results.reason: Issue 3 identifies the automatic five-year renewals under §2.2 and the 270/240-day notice window. It calls this a narrow 30-day window and says missing it means a five-year lock-in.

Issue 1 quotes §3.1: all glass and PET containers, any beverage, worldwide, including Affiliates. It contrasts this with the term sheet's amber glass, beer-only, U.S./Canada scope and treats Harrowgate as contractually bound by the executed text.
Issue 5 cites Recital C and receipt on August 3, 2026. It says the deadline was September 2, 2026, before the September 21 amendment, so the 14% increase is deemed accepted.

Issue 2 explains that the amended §11.2 drops recall costs from the carve-outs and limits the indemnity carve-out to §9.1(c) IP claims. It states recall and product-liability exposure is now subject to the six-month fees cap.

Issue 4 identifies the new §14.4 overriding §14.3 and calls the right unilateral. However, it never says nothing prevents assignment to a competitor, and it does not expressly note that Harrowgate remains bound by the consent requirement.
The response never cites §15.2 or the rule that written amendments take precedence over the Supply Agreement.
Issue 2 states the §11.1 cap is the fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.
The response is a memo addressed to [Partner], with numbered issues. Each issue gives a 'Where' (document and section) and a recommended fix.
The response proposes specific replacement language, including a restored §11.2, a narrowed §3.1 and a revised §2.2.
The response states the increase is deemed accepted and in effect, with no contractual basis left to object.
The response treats §3.1 of the executed agreement as binding and recommends amending it. It does not claim the term sheet governs.
